newsitem.title: UK: Bonds support firm start for Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: Bonds support firm start for Eurobourses.

text.p: European share markets were firmer at midday on Friday, taking support from solid performances by bonds and currencies, and looking to some U.S. data later for potential direction.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average had closed 8.5 points down on Thursday on weak U.S. durable goods orders, failing to give much leadership to Europe.
But London's FTSE 100 index advanced in early trading on Friday, fuelled by sharp gains in the British pharmaceutical sector and a strong gilt and a steady to firm bond market, traders said.
By the middle of the morning the index was up 18 points at the day's high, with advancers leading decliners by a margin of more than five to three.
It later slipped back to around 13 points ahead as gilts gave up a little ground.
Markets were taking more cognisance of some low-key U.S. data later, with the second quarter real domestic product figure due at 1230 GMT and Michigan September consumer confidence data due to 1400.

In Milan, Italian shares were strongly firmer on optimism over the accord struck on Italy's 1997 financial budget which is aimed at putting Italy on track to join a European single currency, dealers said.
Shares were slow to react to the budget news, but were following along in the wake of surging domestic bonds and the lira which has pushed below 1,000 per mark to touch new highs, dealers said.
The all-share Mibtel index was up 2.03 percent at 10,050 and the Mib30 index was 2.35 percent higher at 15,157.

In Paris, French shares started higher, supported by a firm bond market, with stock market analysts saying the trend was bullish. "The market is still far from being technically overbought," said one.
The blue-chip CAC 40 index was up around five points by midday.
Germany bucked the trend somewhat, with shares trading lower at midday, hit by profit-taking ahead of the weekend after the DAX Index reached a new record high on Thursday.
There was support from the German debt market and the strong dollar.

In currencies, the dollar was well supported at European midsession, willing but not able to push higher with the threat of mild profit-taking the only blot on a generally bullish horizon, traders said.

The currency market had half an eye on forthcoming U.S. real GDP data, with most interest in the reaction from U.S. asset markets, eager for evidence that the Federal Reserve was right not to tighten policy this week.
Economists forecast the GDP data, due at 1230 GMT, will show an average 4.6 percent rise, down from the provisional 4.8.
Analysts said the market would also be looking at the minutes of the August 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, due tonight, to see whether the bias remained towards tightening.
But players were already gearing up for the most important indicator, U.S. non-farm payrolls, due to appear next Friday. This will dominate the markets next week, traders and analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5228 marks and 110.63 yen by 1130 GMT, up slightly from late Thursday's European level of 1.5209 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 13.8 points at 3,947.5.
In Paris the CAC-40 share iNdex was down POINTS AT 2,107.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 5.89 points at 2.660.66. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in London at $380.30, vs $380.45 previously.
